author: blu
body: THE REGION IS RESOLVED ONCE AND THREADED. `fact-store-region` takes no arguments, so every mention of it runs again, and each run reads the GPT. Threading the answer is the discipline the store itself follows: `disk-init` and `disk-load` resolve the base once and carry it in the `DiskFactStore` rather than asking per access.

author: blu
body: THE EFFECT ROWS ARE NOT UNIFORM HERE, AND THE SPLIT IS NOT ARBITRARY. `block-read-sector` and `block-sector-count` are builtins that declare `Device.Block`, so anything calling one directly declares it too and binds the result with an act-bind. Everything reached through `DiskFacts` -- `fact-read-at`, `read-superblock`, `fact-store-region` -- declares no row, so the functions built on those declare none either. The boundary belongs to that chapter rather than to this one, and restating it here would be inventing a second answer to a question already settled next door.

author: blu
body: All three states of a region are things an operator has to be able to tell apart, and two of them answer base zero. A whole-disk store really does begin at LBA 0; a refusal reports base -1 and means the disk carries a partition table with no fact partition in it. Printing the number alone would collapse the first into the second.

author: blu
body: The sector count is the drive's own answer, and a stuck counter reports zero for every disk. Zero is also the truthful answer when no disk is attached, so the two are named differently here rather than both printing as a number.

author: blu
body: THE KIND IS REPORTED AS A RAW INTEGER. `int-to-fact-kind` answers CapabilityFact for every value of four or above, so a corrupt or unknown kind would be displayed as a legitimate one. An inspector that renamed the thing it was inspecting would be worth less than no inspector.
